messages:
emma: Quick sync — product asked for a firm plan for v1 -> v2 deprecation that avoids breaking customers and keeps quotas predictable. Two questions: routing + user-facing console UX.

michael: +1. what's the proposed routing behavior during the grace window? prefer v2, but allow v1 fallback?

emma: Thinking: default route to v2 if client sends `x-redwood-api-version: v2`. If header missing, prefer v2 but allow fallback to v1 only when capacity or model-compatibility probes fail. No silent automatic downgrade that changes billing.

sanjay: Important: telemetry needs explicit signals so we can measure who relies on implicit v1 behavior. Suggest emitting `compat_probe` events when fallback happens: `compat_probe:{client_id, from:v2,to:v1,reason}`.

leah: UX: Console should show a per-key compatibility banner + rollout progress: percent of requests upgraded, fallback count, and quota impact. Also a small button to opt a key into "force v1" for enterprise customers during migration.

michael: For quotas — if a request falls back to v1 we should keep token billing semantics consistent with the route that actually served it. But we must flag these in billing telemetry so finance can reconcile any delta.

emma: Agreed. Also: no automatic conversion of embedded-model parameters between versions. If we detect param incompatibility we surface a client error and a short, actionable message: `incompatible-params: upgrade client or add header to force v1`

oliver: Implementation sketch for routing policy (pseudo):
```
routing:
  prefer: v2
  fallback:
    allowed: true
    probe_policy: [schema_check, model_signature, latency_spike]
    sticky_for: 30m
```
This would keep users on the fallback for a short sticky window to reduce churn.

sanjay: Telemetry events to add: `api_version_negotiate`, `compat_fallback_count`, `compat_probe` (as above), `upgrade_adoption_ping` (client pings v2 explicitly). We'll want dashboards with 95/99p latency per route + fallback ratio.

leah: Console banner copy draft: "Heads up — we're rolling v2. Some clients without explicit version headers may be routed to v1 temporarily. See migration guide and opt a key to force v1." Link to docs. Also show per-key sample curl commands including `-H 'x-redwood-api-version: v2'`.

michael: Rollout plan proposal: 1) telemetry-only dry run for 48h (emit logs but don't enforce), 2) soft-pref routing (prefer v2) for 7 days, 3) canary where 5% of traffic is forced to v2, 4) escalate to 25/50/100% with 24h holds. Each step gated by automated health checks (latency, error-rate, compat_fallback_count not rising).

emma: Owner assignments: telemetry + dashboards -> @sanjay, console UI + banners -> @leah, routing + runtime changes -> @michael, rollout coordination + docs -> @emma. Can each owner confirm?

sanjay: sgtm. Will add `compat_fallback_count` to infra metrics and pump to datadog.

leah: I'll mock banner and per-key control in the console repo, add a checkbox `force v1` and an audit log entry.

michael: I'll prepare a routing feature flag behind `feature/api_version_routing_v2` and a lightweight probe implementation. Will also add quota annotation to the request trace.

emma: Nice. Two follow-ups: - Add a 30-day grace period window in docs and a migration checklist. - Add a small sampling probe that returns an example error when v2 param mismatch detected to help client authors.

oliver: deploy-bot: `deploy started` for `api-routing-probe` -> sha: a1b2c3 (this is the probe-only deploy, no enforcement). :rocket:

emma: Perfect. We'll reconvene after the 48h telemetry dry run and decide go/no-go for soft-pref routing. Thanks all :thumbsup:
